Ariestar/sivtr.description: A unified agent memory workspace for human and agent | A unified agent memory workspace
Ariestar/sivtr.body:
A unified memory space for agents and humans, letting agents and terminals share the same context

  ·
  ·
  ·

---

## Why sivtr?

Developers and agents often waste time rebuilding context that already exists: terminal errors, test output, tool logs, earlier AI sessions. `sivtr` turns this local work into searchable memory, without requiring you to adopt a heavy knowledge system.

With `sivtr`, you can:

- Have an agent fix the most recent failure without you pasting logs;
- Recover yesterday's test output, build errors, or key decisions within seconds;
- Jump from a summary back to the original command output or agent reply;
- Save a set of useful results as a variable such as `@failures` and keep using it in the next command.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> For agent workflows, install the `sivtr` CLI, register MCP with `sivtr mcp install`, and optionally use the built-in `sivtr-memory` skill. MCP is the main path for agents to read local evidence; the skill teaches the agent when and how to call it.

## Features

- **MCP-first agent memory**: With a single `sivtr mcp install`, agents directly call the search/show/zoom/filter/status/usage/stats tools, without you pasting logs.
- **Terminal capture with preserved output**: Records commands, stdout/stderr, exit codes, directories, and durations in Bash, Zsh, PowerShell, and Nushell; `pipe` and `run` write directly into the same archive.
- **Unified local archive**: All terminal and agent sessions are first synced into a single `archive.db`. Providers only handle discovery and parsing, while search, filtering, export, TUI, MCP, and Web API share the same record model.
- **40+ agent providers**: Codex / Claude Code / Cursor / Dsh / Gemini / Goose / Hermes / OpenCode / OpenClaw / Grok / Pi / Qoder / Qoder-CN / Qwen, plus more JSONL, SQLite, directory, and container formats, all using the same registry and query surface.
- **Precise evidence, not summaries**: Every hit resolves to a stable ref that can be shown, zoomed, or filtered, or handed to the next agent.
- **Named memory variables**: Save results as `@failures`, reuse `@last`, use `@` in pipes, or take a subset with `@failures[1,3..5]`.
- **Usage and cost**: Extracts token usage from transcripts, using exact integer micro-dollar amounts and built-in pricing…

ChaYeWuu/violin-CVE-2026-98260-OS4.0.description: Gain ROOT access and load KernelSU on a Xiaomi Pad7S Pro12.5 running OS4.0.0.14.XOTCNXM using CVE-2026-98260.
ChaYeWuu/violin-CVE-2026-98260-OS4.0.body:
# XRING-KSU · CVE-2026-98260

One-click root on **Xiaomi Pad 7S Pro 12.5 (violin / 25053RP5CC)**: uses `CVE-2026-98260` (a POSIX timer UAF in the `exec` subsystem) to obtain arbitrary kernel read/write, then ends up with root, permissive SELinux, and the official **KernelSU 3.3.1** loaded. It is packaged as an Android app with a two-pane tablet UI.

> [!WARNING]
> This project rewrites kernel memory, switches SELinux to permissive mode, and loads unsigned kernel modules. It may cause system panics, data loss, or a device that will not boot. Use it only on devices you own, and before running it, confirm that the device model and kernel version match.

---

## Where the window in this CVE is

The core of `CVE-2026-98260` is the cleanup order in `begin_new_exec()` in `fs/exec.c`: `de_thread()` has already swapped the thread's TID out, but `posix_cpu_timers_exit()` only runs after `exec_mmap()` succeeds. If the step in between fails, the timer node is never removed.

```
B thread execve
  └─ de_thread()            swap TIDs; B's pid is handed to the dead leader
  └─ exec_mmap()            mmap_read_lock_killable interrupted by SIGKILL → -EINTR
  └─ begin_new_exec fails   point_of_no_return already set → B is killed
       └─ do_exit → exit_itimers()
            └─ posix_cpu_timer_del()  pid_task(dead leader) == NULL → goto out directly
                                      ⇒ neither disarms nor WARNs
            └─ k_itimer is kfree'd, but the timerqueue node is still on B's tree
parent wait4 → release_task(B) → posix_cpu_timers_exit(B)
            └─ cleanup_timerqueue()  rb_erase on the freed node ⇒ UAF write
```

From the moment `k_itimer` is freed until the parent's `wait4` triggers `rb_erase`, a full process scheduling round sits in between. **The window is under our control** and can last hundreds of milliseconds, which is enough time to reclaim the freed slab page and forge its contents.

Testing turns B into a zombie…

Cyborg2017/midea_smart_home.body:
# Midea Smart Home

Home Assistant local control integration for Midea devices. Control your smart devices without a cloud connection.

## Getting Help

- Join our QQ group for discussion, the latest updates, and help:

## Features

- **Local control**: Devices are controlled directly over the local network and do not depend on a cloud connection
- **Automatic protocol download**: Automatically downloads each device's Lua protocol script from the cloud (first-time setup)
- **Flexible configuration**: Supports customizing entity attributes through device mapping files, making it easy to adapt new devices
- **Multilingual support**: Supports Chinese and English interfaces
- **Rich entity platforms**: Supports binary_sensor, button, climate, cover, fan, humidifier, light, lock, number, select, sensor, switch, text, time, update, vacuum, water_heater

## Workflow

**Configuration stage**

1. User enters Midea account credentials
2. Logs in to the Midea cloud API

**Discovery stage**

1. Fetches device details from the cloud (device ID, model, SN8, etc.)
2. Automatically downloads the Lua protocol file for each device
3. Scans the local LAN for device IP addresses
4. Obtains the device Token and Key (required only for V3 protocol devices, not for V1/V2)

**Runtime stage**

1. Connects to the device over the local network
2. Uses Lua scripts to parse the device protocol
3. Regular devices push state updates via callbacks. Special devices (such as 0xD9 dual-drum washing machines) use periodic polling
4. User actions are sent directly to the device (no cloud involved)

## Requirements

- **Home Assistant** >= 2025.12.4

## Installation

### One-click install (recommended)

### HACS custom repository

1. Open HACS in Home Assistant
2. Go to "Integrations"
3. Click the "+" button in the top right
4. Click "⚙️ Custom repositories" (3-dot menu > Custom repositories)
5. Enter: `https://github.com/Cyborg2017/midea_smart_home`
6. Select category: **Integration**
7. Click "Add"
8. Search for "Midea Smart Home" and click "Download"

### Manual installation

1. Copy the `custom_components/midea_smart_home` directory into your Home Assistant `custom_components` folder
2. Restart Home Assistant
3. Go to Settings > Devices & services
4. Click "Add integration"
5. Search for "Midea Smart Home"

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```

Then select iPhone in Xcode and press `Cmd + R` to install.

Zzz-IT/GoclashZ.description: A modern Mihomo (Clash Meta) proxy client built on Wails v2 and Vue 3, designed to give Windows users a lightweight, high-performance, and visually pure experience.
Zzz-IT/GoclashZ.body: # GoclashZ A high-performance, industrial-grade solid-color aesthetic Mihomo (Clash Meta) desktop controller built on Wails --- GoclashZ was born out of resistance to the bloat of modern desktop applications. This project abandons the traditional Electron architecture and leverages Go's system-level concurrency and Wails' native rendering to compress memory footprint and system resource usage to the physical limit. Visually, it adheres to a minimalist industrial aesthetic of high contrast and solid black-and-white colors, removing all meaningless gradients and decorations. It is not just a control interface, but a network state management system that has undergone rigorous hardening. ## Interface Preview | Dark Mode | Light Mode | | :---: | :---: | | | | | | | | | | ## Core Features ### Network Takeover and Control * **Independent Helper Privilege Architecture**: Introduces a fully isolated local background service (Named Pipe IPC) responsible for securely managing high-privilege operations (TUN mode, UWP loopback exemption, service start/stop). The main program always runs with regular privileges. * **Smart TUN Engine**: Built-in automated deployment and state self-healing for the Wintun virtual network adapter driver. Every 6 hours (Beijing time 05:00, 11:00, 17:00, and 23:00), free GitHub Actions fetches public subscriptions, removes duplicates, tests the nodes in the cloud, and generates complete configurations for FlClash and Clash Meta / Mihomo. # 🚀 V2rayCollector - Smart Node Crawling and Speed Testing Tool

```text…
A fully automated Telegram channel node crawler + subscription link collector + node deduplication + speed testing + subscription conversion tool

[English](https://github.com/jagger235711/V2rayCollector/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Simplified Chinese

---

## 📋 Project Overview

**V2rayCollector** is a powerful, fully automated node collection and management tool that integrates crawling, deduplication, speed testing, and format conversion. It can:

- 🕷️ **Automatically crawl** V2ray node configurations from Telegram channels
- 🔗 **Aggregate and process** nodes from multiple subscription links
- 🧹 **Smart deduplication** with concurrent detection, excluding invalid and slow links
- ⚡ **Efficient speed testing** using singtools for batch node speed tests
- 🔄 **Format conversion** supporting multiple subscription formats based on subconverter
- ⏰ **Automatic updates** running daily on a schedule via GitHub Actions
- 📊 **Categorized output** with results sorted by protocol type

### ✅ Supported Protocol Types

| Protocol | Supported | Notes |
|------|------|------|
| **VLESS** | ✅ | Supports advanced features such as Reality |
| **VMESS** | ✅ | Supports AEAD encryption |
| **Trojan** | ✅ | TLS 1.3 & full encryption |
| **Hysteria2** | ✅ | Next-generation protocol based on QUIC |
| ~~Shadowsocks~~ | ❌ | Low availability, excluded |

---

## 🏗️ Project Architecture

```
Input sources
├─ Telegram channels (channels.csv)
└─ Subscription links (subList.csv)
    │
    ▼
[1] URL validity check (deduplicate.py)

    - Timeout detection (5 seconds)
    - Slow link detection (>1 second)
    │

ximing/vital.body:
# Vital

**A personal operating system built AI First**: Capture (Inbox) → Execute (Todos) → Reflect (Reports).

> [English documentation](https://github.com/ximing/vital/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md)

Vital is a Chinese-first (`zh-CN`), single-user, self-hosted personal productivity system. Todos, read-later items, habits, threads, and reviews live together in one calm workspace. **Internally, a resident Agent organizes, breaks down, drafts, and remembers your preferences for you. Externally, it provides a skill so that Claude, Codex, and other Agents can operate on the same data directly.**

No chasing collaboration, no manufactured anxiety. One account is everything.

| Light | Dark |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

## Product Philosophy

Vital is **AI First** and also pursues **Calm Productivity**. When you open it, you see "what to do next" first, not the system itself. The Agent works in the background and proposes changes that only take effect once you approve them.

- **One closed loop, not a pile of tools.** Drop links into the Inbox first; once read, convert them into tasks with one click. Completed tasks flow automatically into the day's review, and ideas captured in reviews become tomorrow's actions. The Agent discovers threads, breaks down and postpones tasks, drafts plans, generates daily reports, and turns your corrections into long-term memory.
- **Content before containers.** Todos, reading, and reviews are directly operable information rows, not piles of cards. Structure is expressed through layout, hairline rules, and the rhythm of density.
- **Status matters, but doesn't manufacture anxiety.** Overdue items only color the date, never the entire task in red. No red dots, no big KPI numbers.
- **Single user, your data stays yours.** Every row in Postgres is your own data and can be migrated away at any time. LLM keys are configured on demand, and usage and spend are visible on the usage page.

The visual theme is **Emerald Garden**: warm white paper, emerald green, deep ink, and glowing mint in dark mode. The design spec is at [docs/vital-calm-productivity-design-system.md](https://github.com/ximing/vital/blob/HEAD/docs/vital-calm-productivity-design-system.md).

## Agent · Two Paths for AI First

Vital treats the Agent as part of the product, not a bolted-on chat window.

1. **Internal**: the background Agent in the worker observes your tasks, habits, and feedback, runs on its own according to a scheduling policy, and produces proposals you can accept.
2. **External**: the [skills/vital](https://github.com/ximing/vital/blob/HEAD/skills/vital/SKILL.md) in the repository lets other Agents…
